1: Santa Clara rode a spectacular shooting performance from [[espn:41452|Kevin Foster]] to an 83–76 road victory over Pepperdine. The senior guard poured in 29 points, connecting on 11 of 17 shots and six three-pointers. The Broncos shot 53.6% from the floor and hit 12 threes, building a 46–36 halftime advantage behind Foster, [[espn:41455|Marc Trasolini]] (18 points, eight rebounds), and [[espn:46703|Raymond Cowels III]] (15 points, nine rebounds).

Pepperdine refused to go away. Led by [[espn:41442|Lorne Jackson]], who finished with 23 points and five assists, and [[espn:56584|Jordan Baker]], who added 15, the Waves trimmed a 13-point second-half deficit to just two, 68–66, with 4:33 remaining. Foster answered the challenge, eventually burying his sixth three-pointer with 1:11 left to give Santa Clara the breathing room it needed.

[[espn:51845|Evan Roquemore]] orchestrated the Broncos' offense with 10 assists, helping Santa Clara improve to 14–6 overall and 3–3 in West Coast Conference play. Foster's six triples also brought him into a tie for 17th on the NCAA's all-time career three-pointers list at the time. It was a memorable individual performance in a competitive conference road win.
2: San Diego relied on its defense to defeat Robert Morris 65–53 in its home opener at Jenny Craig Pavilion, improving to 2–0 to begin the 2017–18 season. [[espn:3134910|Isaiah Wright]] led the Toreros with 17 points, eight rebounds and six assists, while freshman [[espn:4285624|Yauhen Massalski]] contributed 11 points, eight rebounds and three blocks. USD struggled to find its shooting touch but held the Colonials to 33.3% from the floor.

After taking a narrow 30–27 lead into halftime, San Diego used a 9–0 second-half run, featuring two baskets by [[espn:4066744|Juwan Gray]], to move ahead 42–33. Robert Morris answered with eight straight points from [[espn:4279636|Leondre Washington]] to close within 42–41, but the Toreros maintained their advantage. A corner three from [[espn:3906543|Olin Carter III]] pushed the lead into double figures late, and a Massalski finish off a Wright assist put the result out of reach. Washington scored 15 for the Colonials, while [[espn:3906544|Alex Floresca]] added 10 for USD.
3: San Diego survived a second-half rally from Norfolk State to secure a 71–62 victory and improve to 3–0 for the first time since the 2013–14 season. [[espn:3906543|Olin Carter III]] led the Toreros with 21 points, knocking down five three-pointers, while [[espn:3136521|Cameron Neubauer]] added 16 points and five assists. USD dominated the opening half, holding the Spartans to just 16 points and taking a commanding 38–16 lead into the break.

Norfolk State made things interesting after halftime, gradually cutting the deficit to six points in the closing minute. [[espn:3948866|Nic Thomas]] paced the Spartans with 16 points, while [[espn:3947058|Alex Long]] contributed 14. Carter's timely three-pointer inside the final five minutes helped steady San Diego, and [[espn:3906571|Isaiah Pineiro]], who finished with 14 points and seven rebounds, sealed the win at the free-throw line. The victory marked just the sixth 3–0 start for USD since joining Division I in 1979–80.
4: [[espn:3906571|Isaiah Pineiro]] delivered a dominant all-around performance as San Diego defeated Little Rock 66–52 to improve to 4–0 for just the third time in its Division I history. Pineiro filled the stat sheet with 20 points, seven rebounds, four assists, four steals and two blocks, leading a Toreros team that controlled the game with its defense. USD opened each half with an 11–0 run, while limiting the Trojans to 37.3% shooting and forcing 17 turnovers.

San Diego built a 28–18 halftime lead and stretched its advantage to 20 points midway through the second half. Although the Toreros endured a nearly nine-minute stretch without a field goal, Little Rock never seriously threatened the lead. [[espn:3134910|Isaiah Wright]] contributed 12 points, seven rebounds and five assists, connecting on all three of his three-point attempts, while [[espn:3136521|Cameron Neubauer]] added 11 points. [[espn:4280283|Cameron Corcoran]] led Little Rock with 11 points, making all three of the Trojans' three-pointers.
5: The annual San Diego City Championship brought an undefeated USD team into a rivalry showdown with San Diego State at Jenny Craig Pavilion. The Toreros entered 5–0, looking to establish themselves against their crosstown rivals, but the Aztecs handed them their first defeat of the season, 66–57. [[espn:3136524|Devin Watson]] delivered the game's defining performance, scoring 26 points on 7-of-11 shooting while adding five steals and converting 10 of 11 free throws.

San Diego's offense struggled against the Aztecs' defense. After a promising opening stretch, USD missed 14 consecutive field-goal attempts during an eight-minute drought, allowing SDSU to build a 25–11 advantage. The Toreros fought back to trail 30–22 at halftime, then cut the deficit to just four points, 36–32, early in the second half on a three-pointer by [[espn:3134910|Isaiah Wright]]. San Diego State responded and gradually regained control, pushing its lead to 13 points with just over seven minutes remaining.

[[espn:3906571|Isaiah Pineiro]] led USD with 19 points, five rebounds and three blocks, while [[espn:3906543|Olin Carter III]] added 12 points. The Aztecs received 13 points from freshman [[espn:4278706|Matt Mitchell]] and 11 from [[espn:3906650|Jeremy Hemsley]]. USD finished just 7-of-30 from three-point range, a decisive factor in a game where its defense otherwise kept the contest competitive. San Diego State claimed the city bragging rights, while USD suffered its first setback after a promising start.
6: San Diego's defense overwhelmed Northern Arizona from the opening tip in a 79–51 victory at Jenny Craig Pavilion. The Toreros scored the first 15 points and held the Lumberjacks scoreless for more than eight minutes, eventually building a 26–3 lead. [[espn:3906571|Isaiah Pineiro]] punctuated the early surge with transition dunks, while [[espn:3136521|Cameron Neubauer]] and [[espn:3906543|Olin Carter III]] helped stretch the defense with perimeter shooting. USD led 38–18 at halftime and never faced a serious threat.

Neubauer finished with a season-high 17 points, followed by Pineiro's 16 points and seven rebounds and [[espn:3906542|Tyler Williams]] with 11 points and seven boards. San Diego made a season-high 13 three-pointers and expanded its lead to as many as 33 in the second half. [[espn:3155710|Gino Littles]], [[espn:4066904|JoJo Anderson]] and [[espn:3155501|Torry Johnson]] scored 11 apiece for Northern Arizona. The win moved the Toreros to 7–2, matching their start from the 2013–14 season.
7: A dramatic late comeback was not quite enough for San Diego, which fell 86–83 in overtime to North Texas at Jenny Craig Pavilion. The Mean Green leaned on a sensational 31-point performance from [[espn:4279090|Roosevelt Smart]], while [[espn:3906547|Ryan Woolridge]] added 20 points and seven assists. USD had led by seven in the first half, but North Texas carried a 37–35 advantage into the break and repeatedly answered Torero rallies in the second half.

Trailing 77–72 with 28 seconds remaining in regulation, San Diego suddenly came alive. [[espn:3134910|Isaiah Wright]] made two free throws, and [[espn:3906543|Olin Carter III]] buried a three-pointer with 18 seconds left to tie the game at 77 and force overtime. North Texas moved ahead 85–81 in the extra period before [[espn:3906542|Tyler Williams]] converted two free throws to bring USD within two. After one North Texas free throw, [[espn:4285624|Yauhen Massalski]] deflected the ensuing inbound pass and recovered it, but his desperation three-point attempt in the final seconds missed.

Williams paced five Toreros in double figures with 18 points, followed by [[espn:3906571|Isaiah Pineiro]] with 15 and [[espn:4066744|Juwan Gray]] with 14. USD made 28 of 32 free throws but could not contain Smart and the North Texas offense. The narrow loss dropped San Diego to 8–3, with its last-second chance providing one of the early season's most memorable finishes.
8: San Diego closed its nonconference schedule with a comfortable 94–51 victory over NAIA opponent Life Pacific, improving to 9–3 before West Coast Conference play. [[espn:3134910|Isaiah Wright]] produced a 14-point, 12-assist double-double, finishing just two assists shy of USD's school record. [[espn:3906571|Isaiah Pineiro]] scored a game-high 16 points as the Toreros built a 43–24 halftime lead and steadily widened the gap.

[[espn:3906542|Tyler Williams]] made his first start of the season and joined [[espn:4285624|Yauhen Massalski]] among USD's double-figure scorers. The Toreros recorded 24 assists, shot 52.9% from the field, and blocked 10 shots—one short of the program record—with every available player seeing action. [[espn:3953198|Jonathan Cortez]] led Life Pacific with 15 points, but USD's balanced attack made this a convincing tune-up heading into conference play.
9: No. 13 Saint Mary's arrived at Jenny Craig Pavilion riding a 17-game winning streak, and San Diego nearly delivered a memorable upset. Instead, the Gaels escaped 65–62 behind a towering performance from [[espn:3146557|Jock Landale]], who amassed 34 points, 18 rebounds and four assists on 15-of-22 shooting. The victory extended Saint Mary's winning streak to 18 games and kept the Gaels unbeaten in West Coast Conference play.

The visitors seized control with a 20–3 first-half run, holding USD without a field goal for more than ten minutes and carrying a 36–24 lead into halftime. Landale already had 18 points and 11 rebounds at the break, but the Toreros refused to disappear. [[espn:3906571|Isaiah Pineiro]], who finished with 24 points, helped lead a late rally as USD cut a 12-point second-half deficit to three. With the game on the line, [[espn:3134910|Isaiah Wright]] hit a wing three-pointer with 11 seconds remaining to pull San Diego within 63–62.

[[espn:3090679|Emmett Naar]] calmly made two free throws to restore a three-point Saint Mary's lead, and USD's final attempt to tie fell short. Naar finished with 11 points and seven assists, while [[espn:4066736|Jordan Ford]] supplied two critical baskets down the stretch. [[espn:3906542|Tyler Williams]] added 12 points for San Diego, which came agonizingly close to upsetting one of the nation's best mid-major teams.

For a game remembered as much for the visiting star as the result, Landale's 34-and-18 masterpiece was the defining image: an NBA-caliber center operating at the height of his college powers while a determined home team made him work until the final possession.
10: Pacific erased an early double-digit deficit and pulled away from San Diego for a 67–55 West Coast Conference road win at Jenny Craig Pavilion. The Toreros started fast behind [[espn:3136521|Cameron Neubauer]], whose three first-half three-pointers helped produce an 18–8 lead. But the Tigers fought back: [[espn:4285659|Jahlil Tripp]] tied it at 22, [[espn:3133868|Miles Reynolds]] converted a four-point play to put Pacific ahead, and [[espn:4285657|Roberto Gallinat]] hit a three at the halftime buzzer for a 29–24 advantage.

Pacific opened the second half with a 15–3 surge, stretching the margin to 44–27. San Diego made one late push, closing to 55–50 with just over two minutes remaining, but Gallinat answered with a basket and helped close the game at the foul line. He finished with a game-high 21 points, including three three-pointers, while Tripp posted 17 points, 11 rebounds and four assists. Reynolds added 13 points and five assists as the Tigers completed a regular-season sweep of the Toreros.

[[espn:3906543|Olin Carter III]] led San Diego with 16 points, Neubauer scored 15, and [[espn:3134910|Isaiah Wright]] handed out eight assists. Pacific's 8-for-14 three-point shooting and 19-for-22 free throws helped overcome its slow start, while San Diego fell to 16–11 overall and 7–8 in conference play.
11: San Diego snapped a five-game losing streak against BYU with a 75–62 victory at Jenny Craig Pavilion, led by 20 points and seven rebounds from [[espn:3906571|Isaiah Pineiro]]. The Toreros shot nine-for-21 from three-point range while holding the Cougars to just three makes in 22 attempts beyond the arc. [[espn:3136521|Cameron Neubauer]] added 14 points and three triples, and [[espn:3906543|Olin Carter III]] scored 13, including eight-for-eight at the foul line, as he surpassed 1,000 career points.

Neubauer opened the scoring with a three-pointer, and after BYU briefly moved ahead early, a layup by [[espn:3906544|Alex Floresca]] put San Diego in front for good. USD led 39–28 at halftime and stretched the margin to 44–28 on five quick points from [[espn:3134910|Isaiah Wright]] after the break. BYU cut the deficit to 46–41 midway through the second half, but the Toreros answered with an 8–3 run. When the Cougars again pulled within five at 61–56 with 4:25 remaining, San Diego finished on a 14–6 run to secure the win.

[[espn:4066657|TJ Haws]] and [[espn:3129951|Elijah Bryant]] scored 14 points apiece for BYU, but the visitors shot only 37 percent overall. Wright contributed 11 points for San Diego, which improved to 17–11 overall and 8–8 in West Coast Conference play. The victory ended BYU's three-game winning streak and gave the Toreros a notable conference home win.
12: No. 6 Gonzaga escaped Jenny Craig Pavilion with a 77–72 victory over San Diego, overcoming a three-point halftime deficit and an eight-point second-half hole to clinch at least a share of the West Coast Conference championship. On a night when the Toreros honored senior [[espn:3136521|Cameron Neubauer]], USD made the nationally ranked Bulldogs work for everything. [[espn:3906543|Olin Carter III]] caught fire from deep, hitting five three-pointers on his way to a game-high 21 points. Three straight Carter triples helped turn a 27–27 tie into a San Diego advantage, and a jumper by [[espn:3906542|Tyler Williams]] helped the Toreros take a 37–34 lead into halftime.

Gonzaga finally moved in front midway through the second half when [[espn:4066651|Killian Tillie]] buried a three-pointer for a 52–51 lead. Tillie finished with 17 points and six rebounds, while [[espn:4066648|Rui Hachimura]] supplied 16 points and eight boards. San Diego stayed within striking distance, but four consecutive Hachimura free throws helped Gonzaga take the lead for good with about four minutes left. The Bulldogs' bigger lineup, featuring Tillie, Hachimura and [[espn:66260|Johnathan Williams]] (11 points, nine rebounds and two blocks), tightened the defense and held USD without a field goal for a crucial six-minute stretch late in the game.

The Toreros were within three points on three occasions in the final three minutes but could not complete the upset. [[espn:3134910|Isaiah Wright]] contributed 14 points and six assists, [[espn:3906571|Isaiah Pineiro]] added 14 points and six rebounds, and freshman [[espn:4285624|Yauhen Massalski]] recorded 11 points, seven rebounds and two blocks. San Diego fell to 17–12, while Gonzaga improved to 26–4 and 16–1 in WCC play. The narrow defeat was a striking contrast to the Bulldogs' 58-point win on their previous visit to San Diego.
13: San Diego opened the CollegeInsider.com Postseason Tournament with an 88–72 victory over Hartford at Jenny Craig Pavilion, extending its season under acting head coach Sam Scholl. The Toreros took a 42–35 lead into halftime and produced one of their sharpest offensive performances of the year, shooting 58.2 percent from the field, making 12 three-pointers and matching their season high with 24 assists. Senior [[espn:3136521|Cameron Neubauer]] led six double-figure scorers with 16 points, hitting four threes in what had become an unexpected additional home game.

Hartford refused to fold. A San Diego advantage that had reached 16 points shrank to four with 11:14 remaining, while [[espn:3906571|Isaiah Pineiro]] sat with four fouls. The Toreros steadied themselves and answered with a decisive 20–5 run to put the game away. [[espn:3134910|Isaiah Wright]] directed the offense with 14 points and 11 assists, while [[espn:3906542|Tyler Williams]] scored 15 on 6-of-7 shooting and Pineiro contributed 13.

[[espn:3906543|Olin Carter III]] added 11 points and [[espn:4285624|Yauhen Massalski]] supplied 10 off the bench. For Hartford, [[espn:3917978|Jason Dunne]] scored 16 with four three-pointers, [[espn:3917979|J.R. Lynch]] had 14, and [[espn:3130746|John Carroll]] and [[espn:4066694|Hassan Attia]] each scored 13. The victory moved USD to 19–13 and gave Scholl his first win as a head coach, sending the Toreros into a second-round home matchup with Portland State.
14: San Diego survived a dramatic CollegeInsider.com Tournament second-round game, edging Portland State 67–64 on a three-pointer by [[espn:3906542|Tyler Williams]] with just 0.5 seconds remaining. The Vikings raced ahead 21–11 and led by as many as 12 in the first half. Behind 11 early points from [[espn:66457|Ryan Edwards]] and a pressure defense that forced 13 first-half turnovers, Portland State took a 37–28 lead into the break.

The Toreros answered with a 17–5 surge to begin the second half, fueled by eight points and two three-pointers from [[espn:3906543|Olin Carter III]], and moved in front 43–42 with 15:29 left. The lead changed hands in a tense finish. [[espn:4278655|Deante Strickland]] tied it at 62 with a jumper just over three minutes from the end, and Edwards sank two free throws to make it 64–64 with 1:14 to play. After San Diego missed a three, Edwards had an open look from deep for the lead, but his attempt rimmed out. USD pushed the ball upcourt and found Williams on the right wing for the game-winner.

Williams and Carter each finished with 16 points; Carter made four threes and recorded five steals. [[espn:3136521|Cameron Neubauer]] contributed 13 points and three triples, while [[espn:3906571|Isaiah Pineiro]] added 12 points and six rebounds. Portland State got 18 points and six rebounds from Edwards, 17 points from Strickland, and 10 rebounds from [[espn:4066942|Brandon Hollins]]. The Toreros' 11 made three-pointers helped overcome 13 fewer first-half points than their opponents, and the victory lifted San Diego to 20–13 and into the CIT quarterfinals.
15: Northern Colorado ended San Diego's postseason run with an 86–75 road victory in the CollegeInsider.com Tournament quarterfinals at Jenny Craig Pavilion. The Toreros shot 66.7% in the first half and led 43–38 at the break, with [[espn:3906571|Isaiah Pineiro]] scoring 15 before halftime. The Bears stayed within reach thanks in part to a quick scoring burst from reserve [[espn:66543|Anthony Johnson]], then changed the game after the intermission.

Northern Colorado tied the score at 45 with 16:51 remaining and went ahead 50–48 on a jumper by [[espn:3912832|Jordan Davis]]. An 8–0 run grew into a 15–3 surge that put the Bears in front for good. San Diego's shooting cooled to 41.4% in the second half, and Northern Colorado capitalized on 17 Toreros turnovers, converting them into 22 points. The Bears outscored USD 48–32 after halftime and made their late free throws to finish the comeback.

[[espn:3913584|Andre Spight]] paced Northern Colorado with 26 points and six three-pointers, while Davis posted 21 points, 12 rebounds and four assists. Johnson added 20 off the bench, reaching 1,000 career points during the game. For San Diego, Pineiro finished with 25 points and 10 rebounds, [[espn:3134910|Isaiah Wright]] scored 23 on 8-of-11 shooting with four assists, and [[espn:4066744|Juwan Gray]] supplied 11. The defeat closed the Toreros' season at 20–14, while the Bears advanced to the CIT semifinals.
16: San Diego opened the 2018–19 season with an 83–66 comeback victory over Weber State at Jenny Craig Pavilion, giving Sam Scholl a win in his first season opener as the Toreros' permanent head coach. The Wildcats controlled much of the opening half, building a lead as large as 11 and taking a 32–25 advantage into the locker room. USD had shot just 33 percent from the floor before halftime, but its offense transformed after the break.

A three-pointer from [[espn:3906543|Olin Carter III]] helped ignite San Diego's early second-half rally. The Toreros moved ahead 38–37, then stretched their lead with an 18–6 burst over six minutes as Weber State struggled to keep pace. San Diego scored 58 second-half points on 65 percent shooting, including 7-of-10 from beyond the arc, and ultimately led by as many as 18. The Toreros also controlled the glass 42–31.

[[espn:3906571|Isaiah Pineiro]] led the way with 25 points, 12 rebounds and four steals, while [[espn:3134910|Isaiah Wright]] contributed 13 points and eight assists. Carter added 13 points, [[espn:3906544|Alex Floresca]] scored 12, and [[espn:4285624|Yauhen Massalski]] supplied eight points and 10 rebounds. For Weber State, [[espn:3917311|Cody John]] scored 22 points on 9-of-15 shooting in his return to action after missing the previous season with a back injury; freshman [[espn:4397388|Israel Barnes]] added 12. The result sent USD into its new campaign at 1–0.
17: San Diego overwhelmed San Diego Christian from the opening minutes, racing to a 34–4 lead and cruising to a 95–47 victory at Jenny Craig Pavilion. The Toreros allowed only one Hawks field goal in the first 9:39 and took a commanding 55–24 advantage into halftime. Their lead eventually reached 50 points, and the 95-point output was USD's highest since December 2016.

[[espn:3906543|Olin Carter III]] paced five Toreros in double figures with 21 points on 8-of-11 shooting, including five three-pointers. [[espn:3906542|Tyler Williams]] added 17 points, five threes, six rebounds and a team-high six assists, connecting on four of his first five attempts from long range. [[espn:4066745|Jose Martinez]] scored a career-high 15 points and grabbed nine rebounds, while [[espn:3906571|Isaiah Pineiro]] contributed 12 points, nine rebounds and five assists. [[espn:4285624|Yauhen Massalski]] supplied 12 points off the bench.

USD shot 55 percent overall and 43 percent from three-point range while limiting San Diego Christian to 31 percent shooting. The Toreros used all 13 available players; [[espn:4280217|Akim-Jamal Jonah]], [[espn:4280218|Andrew Ferguson]] and [[espn:4397759|Finn Sullivan]] scored their first collegiate points. [[espn:4072748|Hayden Fredrick]] led the Hawks with 13 points, followed by [[espn:4072750|Derek Novsek]] with 10. The win moved San Diego to 3–1.
18: San Diego earned a hard-fought 70–64 win over Colorado at Jenny Craig Pavilion, rallying after the Buffaloes turned a five-point halftime deficit into an eight-point second-half lead. The Toreros were ahead 35–30 at the break, but Colorado's 12–0 run put the visitors up 45–37 with 12:15 remaining. Freshman [[official:colorado-2018-19:evan-battey|Evan Battey]] fueled that surge on his way to a team-high 18 points, while San Diego struggled to find its offense early in the second half.

[[espn:3906571|Isaiah Pineiro]] took over down the stretch, scoring 15 of his game-high 27 points in the final nine minutes. His three-pointer cut the deficit to 50–46, and a later three-point play tied the game at 54. [[espn:3906543|Olin Carter III]] then found [[espn:4285624|Yauhen Massalski]] for a dunk that gave USD a 56–54 lead with 5:27 to play. Colorado briefly moved back in front, 61–60, on two free throws by [[official:colorado-2018-19:mckinley-wright-iv|McKinley Wright IV]] with 1:56 remaining, but Pineiro answered with the go-ahead dunk at 1:31. The Toreros made all eight of their free throws in the final minute to seal the victory.

Pineiro finished with 27 points and seven rebounds, Carter added 22 points and four three-pointers, and Massalski supplied seven points, 14 rebounds and three blocks. For Colorado, Battey scored 18 and Wright posted 14 points, seven rebounds and six assists; [[official:colorado-2018-19:tyler-bey|Tyler Bey]] added eight rebounds and five blocks. San Diego's work on the offensive glass helped offset its lower shooting percentage, and the victory improved the Toreros to 4–1 while handing the Buffaloes their first loss.
19: San Diego kept its strong start rolling with an 82–68 victory over Cal State Northridge at Jenny Craig Pavilion, improving to 8–2 and matching its best 10-game start as a Division I program. The Matadors briefly led by four early, but the Toreros seized control with a seven-point transition burst sparked by consecutive baskets from [[espn:3906571|Isaiah Pineiro]] and a three-pointer by [[espn:3906543|Olin Carter III]]. San Diego took a 40–24 lead into halftime and never trailed after its early first-half rally.

All five San Diego starters scored in double figures. [[espn:3906544|Alex Floresca]] delivered a career-high 16 points on 7-of-9 shooting, matching Pineiro's 16 points; Pineiro also grabbed seven rebounds. [[espn:3134910|Isaiah Wright]] supplied 15 points and seven assists, Carter scored 13, and [[espn:3906542|Tyler Williams]] added 12 on four three-pointers. The Toreros shot 52.5% from the floor, made 11 threes and recorded 25 assists on 32 field goals.

Cal State Northridge found more offense after halftime, scoring 44 second-half points, but never got closer than 13 after the break. [[espn:4278738|Lamine Diane]] led the Matadors with 19 points and eight rebounds, [[espn:4278736|Terrell Gomez]] scored 13, and [[espn:4397450|Darius Brown II]] handed out 10 assists with four steals. San Diego's balanced attack secured its sixth straight home win to open the season.
20: San Diego answered its earlier postseason loss to Northern Colorado with an emphatic 85–65 win at Jenny Craig Pavilion, improving to 9–3 overall and 7–0 at home. The Bears had eliminated the Toreros in the previous March's CIT quarterfinals, but this rematch turned on an 11–2 San Diego run to close the first half. After [[espn:3912832|Jordan Davis]] hit a three to trim the lead to 28–26 with 3:59 left, the Toreros pulled away for a 39–28 halftime advantage. Reserve [[espn:4280218|Andrew Ferguson]] scored five points during the run, with [[espn:3906571|Isaiah Pineiro]] and [[espn:3134910|Isaiah Wright]] also contributing baskets.

The Toreros shot 56.9% from the field and 8-for-14 from three-point range, with five starters scoring in double figures. [[espn:3906543|Olin Carter III]] led the way with 18 points, Pineiro posted 17 points and 10 rebounds, [[espn:3906542|Tyler Williams]] added 16 points on 7-of-8 shooting, [[espn:3906544|Alex Floresca]] scored 12, and Wright supplied 10 points, seven rebounds and five assists. [[espn:4280214|Joey Calcaterra]] provided a quick four-point burst late in the first half, pairing two layups with a steal between them.

San Diego made 70% of its shots after halftime and pushed its lead to 20 on a Williams three-pointer with 6:30 remaining. The margin peaked at 26 when Carter made a free throw with 3:34 left. Davis finished with a game-high 30 points for Northern Colorado, but needed 26 field-goal attempts; [[espn:3912836|Jonah Radebaugh]] added 16 points and 12 rebounds. The Bears, who entered averaging 93.9 points per game, were held to 65 as the Toreros completed a convincing home victory.
21: San Diego bounced back from its West Coast Conference opening loss with a 73–64 win over Pacific at Jenny Craig Pavilion, improving to 9–0 at home. The Toreros led 31–25 at halftime, then seized control after Pacific scored the first basket of the second half: a 16–0 San Diego run, punctuated by two three-pointers from [[espn:3906543|Olin Carter III]], pushed the margin to 47–27 with 13:41 remaining. [[espn:3906542|Tyler Williams]] also connected from deep during the surge.

[[espn:3906571|Isaiah Pineiro]] led San Diego with 24 points, 11 rebounds and four assists, making all 11 of his free throws for his third consecutive double-double. [[espn:4285624|Yauhen Massalski]] anchored the defense with a career-high seven blocked shots alongside 11 points and nine rebounds; the Toreros recorded 10 blocks as a team. Carter finished with 15 points, including three three-pointers, while reserve [[espn:4280218|Andrew Ferguson]] hit two late first-half threes to help establish the halftime lead.

Pacific narrowed the gap in the closing minutes but could not erase the damage from San Diego's early second-half burst. [[espn:4285659|Jahlil Tripp]] matched Pineiro with 24 points for the Tigers, [[espn:4285657|Roberto Gallinat]] added 19, and [[espn:4285656|Lafayette Dorsey]] scored 15. The victory snapped San Diego's four-game losing streak against Pacific and brought the Toreros to 12–5 overall and 1–1 in conference play.
22: Pepperdine handed San Diego its first home loss of the season, 76–71, at Jenny Craig Pavilion, ending the Toreros' 9–0 start on their own floor. The Waves led 30–26 at halftime and stretched their advantage to eight early in the second half, but San Diego rallied. A layup by [[espn:3906571|Isaiah Pineiro]] put the Toreros ahead with 8:07 left, setting up a back-and-forth finish.

San Diego still held a narrow lead inside the final four minutes, but [[espn:4280201|Colbey Ross]] tied the game at 63 with two free throws, then put Pepperdine ahead for good on a driving basket. [[espn:4397693|Kessler Edwards]] followed with a three-pointer at the 1:54 mark to extend the margin to five. Pepperdine went 10-for-10 at the foul line over the final 3:16, closing out a victory that gave coach Lorenzo Romar his 400th career win.

Ross finished with a career-high 27 points, six rebounds and three assists, while [[espn:3920287|Kameron Edwards]] supplied 23 points and eight rebounds and Kessler Edwards added 13 points. Pineiro paced San Diego with 19 points and five rebounds; [[espn:3906543|Olin Carter III]] scored 12 before leaving with an injury with 10:27 remaining, and [[espn:3906542|Tyler Williams]] and [[espn:4397759|Finn Sullivan]] scored 11 and 10, respectively. [[espn:4280214|Joey Calcaterra]] recorded six assists. The Toreros, already without injured starting guard Isaiah Wright, shot 4-for-18 from three and committed 15 turnovers as they fell to 12–6 overall.
23: San Diego controlled most of the night at Jenny Craig Pavilion, but BYU erased a 14-point second-half deficit to claim an 88–82 overtime victory. The Toreros jumped ahead 18–6 early and carried a 39–30 lead into halftime, then stretched the margin to 51–37 after the break. [[espn:3906543|Olin Carter III]] hit four three-pointers in the opening eight minutes, helping San Diego establish the early advantage.

The Cougars rallied behind [[espn:4066657|TJ Haws]] and [[espn:4066656|Yoeli Childs]], cutting the deficit to 60–59 with 9:48 remaining. [[espn:3917309|McKay Cannon]] drilled a three to give BYU its first lead, 70–69, with under four minutes to play. BYU led 75–73 in the final seconds, but [[espn:3134910|Isaiah Wright]] raced the length of the court for a tying layup with two seconds remaining, forcing overtime.

BYU took charge in the extra period, outscoring San Diego 13–7 as the Toreros missed all three of their overtime field-goal attempts. Haws finished with a career-high 35 points and seven assists, while Childs posted 27 points and 12 rebounds. Cannon added 10 points and three three-pointers. Carter and [[espn:3906571|Isaiah Pineiro]] each scored 20 for San Diego; Pineiro also grabbed 12 rebounds and handed out five assists. [[espn:4285624|Yauhen Massalski]] scored 13, [[espn:3906544|Alex Floresca]] added 12, and Wright had eight points, seven rebounds and seven assists. San Diego led for more than 35 minutes but committed 18 turnovers in the loss.
24: No. 3 Gonzaga met stubborn resistance at Jenny Craig Pavilion, where San Diego held the nation's highest-scoring offense to 30 first-half points and reached halftime tied 30–30. [[espn:3906543|Olin Carter III]] scored 12 of his 14 points before the break, helping the Toreros stay level even as [[espn:3906571|Isaiah Pineiro]] battled foul trouble. But the Bulldogs' defense and transition attack changed the game after intermission.

Gonzaga surged ahead 45–37 early in the second half and later stretched its advantage to 67–52 with 8:30 remaining. [[espn:4066648|Rui Hachimura]] scored 16 of his game-high 22 points after halftime, finishing with 10 rebounds, while [[espn:4066649|Zach Norvell Jr.]] added 18 points and [[espn:3155941|Josh Perkins]] supplied 15 points and nine assists. [[espn:3906665|Brandon Clarke]] contributed 14 points, eight rebounds and two blocks as the Bulldogs shot 20-for-29 (69%) in the second half.

[[espn:3906571|Pineiro]] recovered to lead San Diego with 20 points, including 11 in the final six minutes, and [[espn:3906542|Tyler Williams]] hit four three-pointers on his way to 12 points. The Toreros cut the deficit back to single digits but could not complete the rally, falling 79–67 before a crowd of 5,132. Gonzaga improved to 25–2 overall and 12–0 in West Coast Conference play, extending its winning streak to 16 games.
25: No. 6 Nevada arrived at Viejas Arena with a 24–1 record and a 10-game winning streak, but San Diego State delivered one of the defining upsets of its season, beating the Wolf Pack 65–57 on February 20. The Aztecs seized control with a 15–3 first-half run and carried a 30–21 lead into the break, with [[espn:3906650|Jeremy Hemsley]] scoring 10 of his 15 points before halftime. Nevada, which had not trailed in its previous three games, struggled to find any rhythm against San Diego State's physical defense.

The Aztecs continued to dictate the game after halftime. [[espn:4397368|Aguek Arop]] supplied energy inside, [[espn:4278707|Jordan Schakel]] connected on a timely three-pointer to stretch the lead to 44–32, and [[espn:3136524|Devin Watson]] made two free throws following a technical foul to push the advantage to 52–39 with 9:03 left. San Diego State eventually led by 16 before Nevada mounted a late push.

[[espn:3138160|Caleb Martin]] carried much of Nevada's offense with 20 points and seven rebounds, but [[espn:3148992|Jordan Caroline]] was limited to eight points on 3-of-12 shooting, while [[espn:3138161|Cody Martin]] managed five points on 1-of-7 shooting. The Wolf Pack cut the margin to 60–55 in the final minute after a free throw by [[espn:3133824|Trey Porter]], but Hemsley answered with a layup with 29.6 seconds remaining to help seal the upset.

Watson finished with 15 points, five rebounds and eight assists; Hemsley added 15 points and six rebounds, and [[espn:4066731|Jalen McDaniels]] contributed 10 points and six boards. San Diego State held Nevada to 33.9% shooting and its lowest point total of the season, snapping the Wolf Pack's winning streak and prompting a court-storming celebration. It was the highest-ranked opponent the Aztecs had defeated to that point, a signature home win for Brian Dutcher's team.
26: San Diego broke a three-game losing streak with a 63–52 home victory over Portland at Jenny Craig Pavilion, improving to 17–11 overall and 6–7 in West Coast Conference play. The Toreros carried a 35–30 lead into halftime and made seven three-pointers before the break, but the Pilots remained within reach until San Diego tightened its defense down the stretch.

[[espn:3906571|Isaiah Pineiro]] led the way with 22 points and 16 rebounds, tying his career high on the glass and collecting his 12th double-double of the season. [[espn:3906543|Olin Carter III]] added 16 points, hitting four three-pointers and moving into fifth place on San Diego's career scoring list. Reserve [[espn:4397759|Finn Sullivan]] supplied 11 points and six rebounds, while [[espn:3134910|Isaiah Wright]] distributed a game-high seven assists.

Portland's [[espn:4280209|Tahirou Diabate]] scored a team-high 12 points, but the Pilots managed only 22 points after halftime. San Diego allowed just one Portland field goal and six total points over the final 11:20, closing on a 9–0 run to secure the win. The Toreros finished with 11 made three-pointers and ended the night with a much-needed conference victory.
27: UC Irvine opened the 2019–20 season with a dramatic 76–73 comeback victory at San Diego's Jenny Craig Pavilion on November 5. The Toreros controlled the first half, leading by as many as 18 points and taking a 48–34 advantage into the break. San Diego's early perimeter shooting helped build the cushion, but the Anteaters responded with a much stronger defensive second half.

San Diego still led 61–46 with 13:10 remaining before UC Irvine steadily chipped away. A jumper by [[espn:4066936|Tommy Rutherford]] sparked a 9–0 run, and [[espn:4066932|John Edgar Jr.]] pulled the Anteaters within 62–61 with 5:55 to play. [[espn:4066933|Evan Leonard]] then forced a turnover and converted a fast-break layup for a 65–64 lead with 4:23 left. The teams traded blows in the closing minutes, but Irvine held on, outscoring the Toreros 42–25 after halftime.

Leonard led UC Irvine with 19 points and made all 10 of his free throws, while Rutherford scored 16 on 6-of-7 shooting and [[espn:4279073|Collin Welp]] added 13. For San Diego, [[espn:4067460|Braun Hartfield]] paced the offense with 17 points and eight rebounds, [[espn:4431994|Marion Humphrey]] scored 14, and [[espn:4280214|Joey Calcaterra]] contributed 12. Irvine held San Diego to 6-of-26 shooting in the second half, turning a commanding Toreros halftime lead into a three-point road win.
28: San Diego earned its first victory of the season with a 72–66 overtime win against Fresno State at Jenny Craig Pavilion. The Bulldogs started 12–4, but a 15–2 Toreros run reversed the momentum and San Diego took a 34–28 lead into halftime. [[espn:4280214|Joey Calcaterra]] scored a career-high 21 points, including nine makes in nine trips to the free-throw line, while [[espn:4067460|Braun Hartfield]] and [[espn:4431994|Marion Humphrey]] each added 17.

San Diego led by as many as 13 in the second half before Fresno State fought back to tie the game at 55. [[espn:4593047|Jarred Hyder]], who led the Bulldogs with 23 points, missed a short jumper on the final possession of regulation. In overtime, the Toreros converted four of six field-goal attempts and nine of 11 free throws, scoring 17 points in the extra period. [[espn:3906544|Alex Floresca]] completed a three-point play with 1:15 remaining to push the lead to 67–59.

[[espn:4593797|James Jean-Marie]] supplied 11 points and 11 rebounds for San Diego's first double-double of the season; Floresca added seven rebounds and four assists. For Fresno State, [[espn:4593049|Orlando Robinson]] recorded 12 points and 10 rebounds, and [[espn:3917350|Nate Grimes]] had 10 points and 12 rebounds. San Diego held the Bulldogs to 35.9% shooting and forced 18 turnovers in a hard-earned opening win.
29: San Diego State won the city rivalry matchup 66–49 at Jenny Craig Pavilion, pulling away from San Diego behind a breakout performance from [[espn:4077221|Yanni Wetzell]]. The senior forward scored a career-high 20 points on 9-of-11 shooting and grabbed a career-high 12 rebounds, helping the Aztecs improve to 4–0 and avenge the previous season's loss to the Toreros.

Wetzell scored 13 in the first half as San Diego State built a 34–26 halftime lead. He opened the second half with a hook shot and a three-pointer to stretch the margin to 13, and the Aztecs kept the Toreros at a distance the rest of the way. [[espn:4066668|Malachi Flynn]] and [[espn:4397371|Nate Mensah]] added 10 points apiece for San Diego State.

San Diego was held to 23 second-half points and fell to 2–4. Freshman [[espn:4593795|Noel Coleman]] scored 10 points, while [[espn:4593797|James Jean-Marie]] supplied 10 points and 10 rebounds. The Aztecs' interior advantage and Wetzell's efficient scoring proved decisive in a 17-point road win.
30: San Diego erased a four-point halftime deficit to defeat Hofstra 79–69 at Jenny Craig Pavilion in the opening game of the Boca Raton Beach Classic. The Toreros trailed 40–36 at the break but outscored the Pride 43–29 in the second half, ending a three-game losing streak. [[espn:4067460|Braun Hartfield]] delivered a career-high 25 points and 12 rebounds for his first double-double as a Torero, shooting 10-of-18 from the floor.

[[espn:4280214|Joey Calcaterra]] added 21 points, including three three-pointers, and handed out five assists, while [[espn:4431994|Marion Humphrey]] contributed 11 points and six rebounds. San Diego took the lead early in the second half and tightened its defense, holding Hofstra to 10-of-34 shooting after halftime. The Toreros committed only seven turnovers.

Hofstra closed within 62–59 on a basket by [[espn:4278066|Isaac Kante]] with about four minutes remaining, but late three-pointers from Hartfield and Calcaterra restored San Diego's cushion. [[espn:4067241|Elijah Pemberton]] led the Pride with 28 points and eight rebounds; San Diego's stronger second half secured its third win of the season.
31: UC Irvine handed previously unbeaten Eastern Michigan its first loss of the season, winning 77–56 at the Bren Events Center behind a spectacular shooting performance from [[espn:4279073|Collin Welp]]. The sophomore scored a career-high 31 points on 12-of-14 shooting, including seven three-pointers in nine attempts, and added six rebounds and four assists. The victory improved the Anteaters to 5–4 and dropped the Eagles to 6–1.

The Anteaters led 33–27 at halftime after Welp hit three consecutive three-pointers during a personal nine-point burst. Eastern Michigan closed to 35–34 early in the second half, but UC Irvine answered with a 7–2 run and later broke the game open with 16 unanswered points, extending its advantage to 67–44. [[espn:4066934|Eyassu Worku]] scored 11 points, while [[espn:4066933|Evan Leonard]] added nine.

[[espn:3130580|Boubacar Toure]] paced Eastern Michigan with 14 points and 12 rebounds, but the Eagles shot just 30.5% from the floor. UC Irvine made 14 three-pointers and outrebounded its visitors 44–34. The evening also featured the halftime retirement of former UC Irvine star Scott Brooks' No. 12 jersey, making Welp's career night part of a memorable celebration at the Bren.
32: San Diego closed the Boca Raton Beach Classic with a 68–51 home victory over Holy Cross at Jenny Craig Pavilion. The Toreros led 37–26 at halftime and kept the Crusaders at arm's length throughout the second half, holding a double-digit lead for the final 12 minutes. The win improved San Diego to 4–7 and dropped Holy Cross to 1–8.

Returning after roughly a month away with an injury, [[espn:4285624|Yauhen Massalski]] gave San Diego a lift off the bench with a team-high 12 points and eight rebounds. [[espn:4067460|Braun Hartfield]] added 11 points and six rebounds, while [[espn:4397759|Finn Sullivan]] scored 10 in his first start of the season. The Torero reserves combined for 33 points, their highest bench total of the season to that point.

[[espn:4432092|Joe Pridgen]] led Holy Cross with 16 points and nine rebounds, and [[espn:4280070|Austin Butler]] collected 13 rebounds to go with nine points. San Diego limited the Crusaders to 37.9% shooting and just 51 points, its fewest allowed against a Division I opponent in nearly two years.
33: San Diego rallied from a 25–21 halftime deficit to beat UC Davis 58–54 at Jenny Craig Pavilion, earning its third consecutive victory. Neither offense found much rhythm early, but the Toreros tightened their defense down the stretch, holding the Aggies to just one field goal in the final seven minutes. A late 12–2 surge helped San Diego turn a narrow deficit into a four-point win.

[[espn:4280214|Joey Calcaterra]] and [[espn:4067460|Braun Hartfield]] shared San Diego's scoring lead with 11 points each. Calcaterra made five of six free throws in the final minute to protect the lead, while Hartfield added six rebounds and four assists. [[espn:4397759|Finn Sullivan]] scored 10 off the bench, including a pivotal three-pointer that preceded a Hartfield three as San Diego moved ahead 47–43 midway through the second half.

[[espn:4431994|Marion Humphrey]] grabbed a career-high 12 rebounds as the Toreros won the rebounding battle 36–29. [[espn:3919349|Joe Mooney]] led UC Davis with 14 points, and [[espn:4432077|Elijah Pepper]] contributed nine points and 10 rebounds. San Diego held the Aggies to 31% shooting overall and 4-of-19 from three-point range, overcoming its own 4-of-22 three-point shooting to secure the win.
34: UC Irvine closed 2019 with a 69–56 victory over Pacific at the Bren Events Center, building a 35–25 halftime lead and stretching the margin to 21 early in the second half. The Anteaters used a 21–5 first-half run to seize control, then opened the second period with a 13–2 burst to go ahead 48–27.

Pacific refused to fold. [[espn:4285659|Jahlil Tripp]] helped spark a comeback that cut the deficit to 50–44, and [[espn:3946030|Gary Chivichyan]] later banked in a three-pointer to bring the Tigers within 56–53 with three minutes remaining. UC Irvine held Pacific to three points the rest of the way to preserve the win.

[[espn:4279073|Collin Welp]] led UC Irvine with 17 points, eight rebounds and four three-pointers, while [[espn:4066936|Tommy Rutherford]] added 10 points. [[espn:4066934|Eyassu Worku]] contributed nine points, seven rebounds and five assists. Tripp finished with 14 points and 15 rebounds, and Chivichyan scored 14 for Pacific. The Anteaters shot 7-for-13 from three-point range while limiting the Tigers to 2-for-13.
35: Top-ranked Gonzaga overwhelmed San Diego 94–50 at Jenny Craig Pavilion, taking command almost immediately in a West Coast Conference matchup. The Bulldogs raced to a 53–16 halftime lead, using transition offense and interior scoring to turn the game into a rout. Gonzaga scored 34 points in the paint before halftime and held the Toreros to six first-half field goals.

[[espn:4397667|Filip Petrusev]] scored 15 of his 17 points in the opening half, while [[espn:4280150|Joel Ayayi]] finished with a team-high 20 points, six rebounds and three assists. [[espn:3947074|Admon Gilder]] added 12 points, [[espn:4280151|Corey Kispert]] scored 10, and [[espn:3906547|Ryan Woolridge]] supplied eight points and six assists as Gonzaga repeatedly converted stops into fast-break chances.

San Diego's offense struggled against the Bulldogs' pressure. [[espn:4067460|Braun Hartfield]], [[espn:4278606|Jared Rodriguez]] and [[espn:4285624|Yauhen Massalski]] shared the Toreros' scoring lead with nine points each; Hartfield also grabbed seven rebounds. Gonzaga improved to 17–1 and 3–0 in conference play, while San Diego fell to 7–11 and 0–3 in the WCC.
36: No. 7 San Diego State remained unbeaten with an emphatic 83–65 victory over Boise State at Viejas Arena, using a blistering start to seize control of the Mountain West matchup. [[espn:3936174|KJ Feagin]] hit three early three-pointers and scored 16 of his season-high 23 points before halftime, while [[espn:4066668|Malachi Flynn]] helped fuel the opening burst. The Aztecs led 48–25 at the break after an 18–2 run turned an eight-point advantage into a commanding cushion.

Feagin finished with five three-pointers according to the archived player box score, while [[espn:4077221|Yanni Wetzell]] supplied 20 points, five rebounds and four assists. Flynn added 19 points and six assists, and [[espn:4278706|Matt Mitchell]] contributed 10 points and seven rebounds. Boise State received 16 points and nine rebounds from [[espn:4397266|RJ Williams]], but its 18 turnovers made a comeback difficult.

The Broncos scored 40 second-half points, yet San Diego State's huge first-half margin held up. The Aztecs improved to 17–0 overall and 6–0 in Mountain West play, extending their best start since the 2010–11 season. 37: Santa Clara took command early at Jenny Craig Pavilion, building a 38–17 halftime lead on its way to a 65–52 West Coast Conference win over San Diego. [[espn:4280250|Josip Vrankic]] led the Broncos with 20 points and nine rebounds, and [[espn:4593803|Jalen Williams]] added 11 points, five rebounds and three assists. 38: San Francisco turned a five-point halftime lead into a 69–44 rout of San Diego at Jenny Craig Pavilion. 39: Saint Mary's escaped Jenny Craig Pavilion with a 66–60 victory over San Diego, reaching 20 wins on the season after a tightly contested West Coast Conference matchup. [[espn:4066736|Ford]] played all 40 minutes and finished with 19 points and six assists. [[espn:4066467|Malik Fitts]] supplied 17 points and 14 rebounds before fouling out late, and [[espn:3936192|Tanner Krebs]] scored 10. [[espn:4067460|Braun Hartfield]] led San Diego with 18 points, five rebounds and five assists. [[espn:4285624|Yauhen Massalski]] added 10 points and nine rebounds, while [[espn:4397759|Finn Sullivan]] scored 10. 40: San Diego survived a back-and-forth West Coast Conference contest at Jenny Craig Pavilion, beating Portland 88–81 in double overtime. The Toreros led 30–22 at halftime, but the Pilots scored 46 points in the second half and held a late lead. 41: Pacific finished the 2019–20 regular season with a 71–64 road victory over San Diego at Jenny Craig Pavilion. The Tigers led 36–33 at halftime and outscored the Toreros 35–31 in the second half, completing a seven-point West Coast Conference win. [[espn:4067460|Braun Hartfield]] paced San Diego with 17 points. 42: San Diego opened its 2021–22 season with a commanding 103–38 victory over Division III La Verne at Jenny Craig Pavilion. The Toreros led 49–17 at halftime and added 54 more points after the break, giving the home crowd a lopsided opening-night win.

[[espn:4278701|Vladimir Pinchuk]] paced San Diego with 15 points and seven rebounds off the bench. [[espn:4278018|Terrell Brown-Soares]] contributed 13 points, six rebounds and three blocks, while [[official:san-diego:jase-townsend|Jase Townsend]] also scored 13. 43: San Diego defeated UC Riverside 74–62 at Jenny Craig Pavilion, overcoming an early Highlanders surge to improve to 3–1. Riverside held a six-point lead in the first half, but the Toreros answered with an 11–0 run and took a 36–25 advantage into halftime.

[[espn:4280214|Joey Calcaterra]] led all scorers with 21 points, and [[espn:4397124|Marcellus Earlington]] added 16 for San Diego. [[espn:4278018|Terrell Brown-Soares]] collected 12 rebounds as the Toreros shot 50 percent from the field and made five of their 11 three-point attempts.

UC Riverside stayed within reach behind [[espn:4592979|Zyon Pullin]], who recorded 20 points and 10 rebounds, and [[espn:4397619|Callum McRae]], who finished with 16 points and four assists. A corner three from [[espn:4293886|Flynn Cameron]] cut San Diego's lead to 52–47 with 7:36 left, but the Toreros responded and restored a double-digit cushion before closing out the 12-point victory.
44: San Diego State rallied from a nine-point second-half deficit to edge Arizona State 65–63 at Viejas Arena. The Sun Devils led 30–28 at halftime and stretched their advantage to 39–30 before the Aztecs answered with a 12–0 run, sparked by three-pointers from [[espn:4433183|Lamont Butler]] and [[espn:4278704|Adam Seiko]] and a putback dunk by [[espn:4397371|Nate Mensah]].

[[espn:4279451|Jackson]] paced Arizona State with 16 points, seven rebounds and seven assists, while [[espn:4278134|Kimani Lawrence]] contributed 14 points and 12 rebounds.
45: Cal State Fullerton erased an 18-point first-half deficit and stunned San Diego 57–55 at Jenny Craig Pavilion. The Toreros led by 18 with just over four minutes remaining before halftime, but a three-pointer from [[espn:4702487|Dante Maddox Jr.]] just before the break cut the margin to nine. 46: San Diego State survived a stubborn challenge from UT Arlington, winning 68–62 at Viejas Arena after a tightly contested first half.
